items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the veterans' services law, in relation to expanding the
veterans' services commission
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S9851

SPONSOR: SCARCELLA-SPANTON
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the veterans' services law, in relation to expanding the
veterans' services commission

 
PURPOSE:

The purpose of this bill is to improve the operation of the veteran's
services commission.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 Section 3 of the Veterans' Services Law is amended by:

Increasing the number of members of the. Commission from thirteen to
fifteen, thirteen being veterans.

Requiring the Governor to consider the following appointees: members of
congressionally chartered veterans' service organizations or organiza-
tions approved by the U.S. Secretary of Veterans Affairs pursuant to 38
USC Section 5903, the governor may solicit nominations for appointment
having a presence in NYS; directors of local veterans' service agencies
or their designees; family members of veterans or service members; and
individuals having substantial training, professional experience or
knowledge in any of the following: US Department of Veterans Affairs;
health care, including mental health care; career and employment
services or business management; housing assistances and homelessness;
and/or legal issues unique to veterans including USDVS benefit claims
and appeals and veterans treatment court;

Increasing the number of ex officio members to include the commissioner
of health; the commissioner of mental health; the commissioner of homes
and community renewal, the commissioner of labor and the commissioner of
education

Requiring the commission to meet at least quarterly; Expanding the
powers of the commission to include studying issues of concern to veter-
ans, service members and their families, receiving reports from relevant
State agencies regarding their activities related to veterans and mili-
tary families and submitting an annual report to the Governor and the
Legislature; and maintaining and regularly updating a page on the
Department's website regarding the Commission including all the commis-
sion's minutes and agendas.

Section 2: Effective Date

 
JUSTIFICATION:

The Veterans' Services Commission was first established in 1945.
Although the Commission's membership has changed over time, its mission,
has always been the same, to advise the head of DVS on matters of policy
concerning veterans' issues and to coordinate State programs related to
veterans' affairs. The division became a department on April 1, 2023,
and at that time no changes were made to the Commission. The time now
seems appropriate to make changes.

This legislation seeks to improve the operation of the commission and
make it a more useful tool to the Commissioner of Veterans Services in
formulating policies and coordinating services for the veterans and
military families by requiring the commission to hold regular meetings
and delineating new powers and responsibilities of the commission,
including studying issues of concerns to veterans, service members and
their families. This bill would also allow new perspectives to be
represented in the commission's work by increasing its membership to
allow for the appointment of individuals with useful experience and
expertise such as the family members of service members and veterans as
well as additional ex office members representing relevant state agen-
cies.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

This is a new bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

TBD.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.
